newsitem.title: USA: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended down sharply Tuesday in an active session, with long liquidation and technical selling pressuring the complex despite reports of firmer physical prices, market sources said.
September slumped 11.1 cents to close at $2.475 per million British thermal units. October settled 10 cents lower at $2.478. Most others ended down a half to 7.7 cents.
"This was a correction. It was not overdue but it was due though I still think there's a lot of support in the low-$2.40s (for September)," said one East Coast trader.

With open interest climbing to record levels this week amid a sharp move up, traders said longs, likely nervous ahead of Wednesday's weekly inventory report, opted to take profits, particularly with little weather support on the horizon.
Cooler-than-normal weather is expected to cover most of the East and Midwest this week, while heat continues in much of the Southwest, according to Weather Services Corp.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report range from 60 to 90 bcf versus an 80 bcf build for the same week last year.

Technical traders raised the possibility of a double top today, as September's climb to $2.604 last night on ACCESS just failed to breach the new contract high of $2.605 set yesterday. They pegged support at $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27. Resistance was first seen at the new high of $2.605, with further selling likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January.
In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices were up a couple of cents to the low-$2.50s. Midcon pipes were unchanged in the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas was up slightly to the mid-$2.70s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip slipped 6.2 cents to $2.358. NYMEX said 60,845 contracts traded, down from Monday's revised tally of 66,934.

On KCBT, September finished 10.5 cents lower at $2.375, while deferreds ended down seven to 15 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 10.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 372 lots traded, down from Monday's total of 717.
